items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: Integers \(n,d\geq2\) and a smoothness \(0<s\leq1\); unit indices \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), coordinate indices \(j,\ell\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), component dimension \(p\in\{1,2\}\), and \(B=\binom d2\). Functions \(m:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R\) are finite-valued Borel, square-integrable and centered under Lebesgue measure on the cube; their canonical main and pair effects \(g_j(m)\), \(g_{j\ell}(m)\) are obtained by integrating out the remaining coordinates. For a cube function \(g\) on \([0,1]^p\), \(N_{p,s}(g)^2\) is the infimum over whole-space square-integrable extensions \(G\) of \(\int_{\mathbb R^p}|\mathcal F_pG(\omega)|^2(1+\|\omega\|_2^2/p)^s\,d\omega\), with the unitary Fourier transform \(\mathcal F_p\). The outcome class \(\mathcal H_{d,s}\) collects the centered functions with an exact order-two decomposition and pooled budget \(\sum_jN_{1,s}(g_j(m))^2+\sum_{j<\ell}N_{2,s}(g_{j\ell}(m))^2\leq1\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: Causal completion: with \(\tau_0=0.2\), \(\delta=0.1\), \(\tau(x)=\tau_0+\delta\sqrt2\sin(2\pi x_1)\) and noise \(\epsilon\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,I_{2n})\), the potential outcomes are \(Y_i(1)=m(X_i)+\tau(X_i)/2+\epsilon_{i1}\) and \(Y_i(0)=m(X_i)-\tau(X_i)/2+\epsilon_{i0}\), drawn before assignment and held fixed; \(A_i=(Z_i+1)/2\). The finite-population target is \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}\), with \(\theta=\mathbb E\theta_n\); the Horvitz--Thompson estimator is \(\widehat\theta=\frac2n\sum_iZ_iY_i(A_i)\); \(q_i=\{Y_i(1)+Y_i(0)\}/2\), \(C_\pi(X)=\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(Z\mid X)\), and \(V^*=\delta^2+4=4.01\). The published law class \(\mathcal Q_{d,s}\) consists of laws of a covariate \(U\) uniform on \([0,1]^d\) and square-integrable potential outcomes \(O(0),O(1)\) whose prognostic function \(\mathbb E[(O(1)+O(0))/2\mid U]\) is exactly order-two with zero intercept and pooled budget at most one.

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: Spectral construction: \(\mathbb T_2^r=[0,2)^r\) with addition modulo two and normalized Haar probability; the fold \(b_r(y)_h=\min\{y_h,2-y_h\}\); the even periodic extension \(F=m\circ b_d\); integer frequencies \(k\in\mathbb Z^d\) with characters \(e_k(y)=e^{\mathrm i\pi k^{\mathsf T}y}\), coefficients \(\widehat F(k)=2^{-d}\int_{[0,2)^d}F(y)e^{-\mathrm i\pi k^{\mathsf T}y}dy\), and complexity \(t(k)=\|k\|_2^2/|\operatorname{supp}(k)|\); the ordered real feature sequence \((\phi_h)_{h\geq1}\) of cosine/sine pairs for frequencies with support size one or two, ordered by \(t(k)\) then lexicographically. Independent fair reflection coins \(\eta_{ij}\), lifted covariates \(\widetilde X\), an independent Haar shift \(T\), and \(W_i=\widetilde X_i+T\pmod2\). The single kernel \(\pi^\star_{n,d}\) assigns independent fair signs when \(B\geq n\) and otherwise applies ordered boundary rounding to the first \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) feature rows evaluated at \(W\); \(a_s(n,d)=\min\{1,(B/n)^s\}\).

items.label: Setup S-5
items.nl: Lower-bound prior: a cutoff \(L\geq1\), \(M=BL^2\) pair-cosine coordinates indexed by \(\alpha=(j,\ell,a,b)\) with \(j<\ell\) and \(a,b\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\), features \(V_\alpha(x)=2\cos(\pi ax_j)\cos(\pi bx_\ell)\), uniform independent signs \(\xi\in\{-1,+1\}^M\) drawn independently of \(X\), \(C_0=\sqrt{48+32\pi^2}\), and \(m_\xi=(C_0L^s\sqrt M)^{-1}\sum_\alpha\xi_\alpha V_\alpha\), with law \(\nu^\star_{n,d,s}\). The comparison scale is \(b_s(n,d)=\min\{1,(B/n)^s\}\), with constants \(c_s=2/((48+32\pi^2)16384^s)\) and \(C_s=3072\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal H_{d,s}=\{m:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R:\ m\text{ is finite-valued Borel and centered in }L^2,\ \text{conditions of ass:order-two and ass:pooled-budget hold at }(d,s)\}\). Canonical component equalities and centering are interpreted almost everywhere; arbitrary null-set representatives give the same risk.

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathcal D_{n,d,s}=\{\pi:[0,1]^{nd}\to\mathcal P(\mathcal Z_n):\ \pi\text{ is a Borel probability kernel satisfying ass:fair and ass:assignment-independence at }(n,d,s)\}\). A kernel uses all original units and receives covariates but no function values, pilot outcomes, or unknown outcome model.

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: Draw \(\xi\) before \(X\) and form \(m_\xi\) by the symbol-table formula, with \(L=\max\{1,\lceil\sqrt{4096n/B}\rceil\}\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: Derive \((a_s,\pi^\star,\nu^\star)\) by ordered-prefix nullspace rounding of the real features evaluated at \(W\), with asymmetric boundary-hit probabilities calibrated through conditional zero mean and projected second moments. Use the even extension \(F\) and the independent common shift \(T\) to control cross-frequency terms. For the converse, start from \(V\) and an independent coefficient prior, controlling the expected minimum over the original sign vectors rather than a population eigenvalue count.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: Use the pre-assignment potential-outcome array \(Y\), treatment \(A\), and actual estimator \(\widehat\theta\), targeting \(\theta_n\) conditionally on the realized full schedule and \(\theta\) under the sampling law.

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl:
For an input real matrix \(a\in\mathbb R^{K\times n}\), where \(K=\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), define the following finite randomized map, with fractional state \(u\in[-1,1]^n\) initially zero. A coordinate is active exactly when \(|u_i|<1\); inactive coordinates never move. At a phase start let \(r\) be the number active. If \(r\leq3\), round the remaining coordinates independently to \(+1\) with probabilities \((1+u_i)/2\) and to \(-1\) otherwise, in increasing index order, and stop. If \(r\geq4\), set \(q_1=\lfloor r/4\rfloor\) and retain this value until the active count is at most \(\lfloor r/2\rfloor\). At each move of this phase, let \(P\) be the orthogonal projection onto the vectors supported on the current active set and orthogonal to the first \(q_1\) input rows. Choose its orthonormal basis \(v_1,\ldots,v_h\) by processing \(Pe_1,\ldots,Pe_n\) in index order, discarding zero Gram--Schmidt residuals and normalizing positive residual norms. To compute \(P\), first orthonormalize the restricted constraint rows by the same ordered rule and subtract their rank-one projections from the identity on the active coordinate subspace. For each basis vector set
\[\delta_b^+=\min\left(\left\{\frac{1-u_i}{(v_b)_i}:(v_b)_i>0\right\}\cup\left\{\frac{1+u_i}{-(v_b)_i}:(v_b)_i<0\right\}\right),\]
\[\delta_b^-=\min\left(\left\{\frac{1+u_i}{(v_b)_i}:(v_b)_i>0\right\}\cup\left\{\frac{1-u_i}{-(v_b)_i}:(v_b)_i<0\right\}\right),\qquad t_b=\delta_b^+\delta_b^-,\quad S=\sum_{b=1}^h t_b^{-1}.\]
Only active nonzero entries occur in these sets. Choose \(b\) with probability \(t_b^{-1}/S\). Then replace \(u\) by \(u+\delta_b^+v_b\) with probability \(\delta_b^-/(\delta_b^++\delta_b^-)\), and by \(u-\delta_b^-v_b\) otherwise. Start a new phase when the stopping active count is reached. The terminal output is \(Z=u\in\mathcal Z_n\). Every choice uses an independent uniform seed; inverse distribution functions use half-open intervals, with the value one assigned to the last interval. Comparisons with zero and all boundary comparisons are exact; ties in finite minima use the least index. This definition names the procedure. Its well-definedness, termination, measurability and bounds are proved in the accompanying rounding lemma.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: Lemma 1. There is a choice of \(C_0=C_0(s)\), independent of \(n,d,L\), for which every realization of \(m_\xi\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_{d,s}\). For every \(L\geq1\), \(\mathbb E[V(X_1)V(X_1)^{\mathsf T}]=I_M\), including pair features sharing an original coordinate.

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: Lemma 2. For \(p=1,2\), even period-two reflection maps the cube restriction norm \(N_{p,s}\) into the torus Fourier norm with a constant depending only on \(s,p\). In particular, for every \(m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}\), \[\sum_{1\leq|\operatorname{supp}(k)|\leq2}(1+\pi^2t(k))^s|\widehat F(k)|^2\leq C_s.\] Under the reflection and shift construction, \(W\) is an independent Haar sample independent of \(T\). For any Borel assignment kernel depending only on \(W\) and fresh independent seeds, \[\mathbb E\Big|\sum_i Z_i m(X_i)\Big|^2=\sum_k|\widehat F(k)|^2\mathbb E\Big|\sum_i Z_i e_k(W_i)\Big|^2.\] The identity holds for the finite-valued Borel representatives in the class, by an \(L^2\) approximation argument.

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Lemma 3. For every \(m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}\) and \(\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}\), conditional on the realized full potential-outcome schedule,
\[
 \mathbb E_\pi[\widehat\theta\mid X,Y]=\theta_n,
 \qquad
 n\operatorname{Var}_\pi(\widehat\theta\mid X,Y)
 =\frac4n q^{\mathsf T}C_\pi(X)q.
\]
Under the frozen sampling and Gaussian noise law, \(\theta=0.2\), \(V^*=4.01\), and
\[
 n\operatorname{Var}_{X,Y,Z}(\widehat\theta)-V^*
 =\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi,m).
\]
This pointwise identity transfers the comparison scale and the single \(s\)-independent attaining kernel \(\pi^\star_{n,d}\) of Theorem \texttt{thm:log-free-bivariate-capacity} to actual HT ATE excess variance. For arbitrary square-integrable outcome laws in the frozen uniform class \(\mathcal Q_{d,s}\), the law-level identity and exact-capacity transfer are those of Lemma \texttt{lem:published-prognostic-capacity}.

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
Let \(r_0\) be a local positive integer, and let \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) be independent copies of a random vector \(v\in\mathbb R^{r_0}\) with \(\mathbb E[vv^{\mathsf T}]=I_{r_0}\). No coordinate independence is required. Then
\[\mathbb E\min_{z\in\{-1,1\}^n}\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n z_i v_i\right\|_2^2\geq nr_0-n^2-16n\sqrt{nr_0}.\]
In particular, if \(r_0\geq4096n\), the left hand side is at least \(nr_0/2\).

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
For every ordered collection of deterministic rows \(a_1,a_2,\ldots\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(|(a_h)_i|\leq\Lambda<\infty\), the procedure in the ordered boundary-rounding definition, supplied only the first \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) rows, is Borel, uses at most \(n\) moves, and satisfies
\[\mathbb E[Z_i]=0\quad(1\leq i\leq n),\qquad\mathbb E(a_h^{\mathsf T}Z)^2\leq32\Lambda^2\min\{h,n\}\quad(h\geq1).\]
No full-rank or general-position premise on the row matrix is required.

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
For a local single-unit law \(P\), write \(U\) for its covariate and \(O(0),O(1)\) for its potential outcomes. Its causal target is \(\vartheta(P)=\mathbb E_P[O(1)-O(0)]\). Write \(m_P(u)=\mathbb E_P[(O(1)+O(0))/2\mid U=u]\) for a finite-valued Borel version of its prognostic function. With independent copies across the original \(n\) units, the actual HT estimator and its excess are
\[
 \widehat T_P=\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iO_i((Z_i+1)/2),\qquad
 \mathcal V_n(\pi,P)=n\operatorname{Var}_{P,\pi}(\widehat T_P)-\mathsf V(P),
\]
where \(\mathsf V(P)\) is the conditional-variance expression in Lemma \texttt{lem:published-ht-excess-identity}. Then the frozen uniform, zero-intercept, correctly specified class satisfies
\[
 \{m_P:P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s}\}=\mathcal H_{d,s}
 \quad\text{modulo Lebesgue null representatives}.
\]
It has exactly the admissible fair original-sample Borel kernel class \(\mathcal D_{n,d,s}\), and the stated Gaussian completions form a proper law subclass of \(\mathcal Q_{d,s}\). For every \(\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}\),
\[
 \mathcal V_n(\pi,P)=\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi,m_P),\qquad P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s},
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s}}\mathcal V_n(\pi,P)
 =\sup_{m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}}\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi,m),
 \qquad
 \inf_{\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s}}
       \mathcal V_n(\pi,P)=R_s(n,d).
\]
For comparison, let the local class \(\mathcal A_{d,s}\) be the larger correctly specified, no-priority-block, order-two class of Cytrynbaum's Theorem B.8(ii), with the same component norm convention, its original second-moment and prognostic \(L^2\) bound, its permitted intercepts, and covariate densities \(f\) satisfying fixed bounds \(0<\lambda\leq f(u)\leq\Lambda<\infty\), where \(\lambda\leq1\leq\Lambda\). Then, for all \(n,d\geq2\) and \(0<s\leq1\),
\[
 \inf_{\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal A_{d,s}}
       \mathcal V_n(\pi,P)
 \geq R_s(n,d)\geq c_s b_s(n,d),
 \qquad
 c_s\geq\frac{2}{(48+32\pi^2)16384}>0.
\]
Consequently, for each fixed \(s\), vanishing worst-case excess on this larger class along any integer sequence \(d=d_n\geq2\) requires \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\).

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
For \(p\in\{1,2\}\), \(0<s\leq1\), and a cube function \(g\in L^2([0,1]^p)\) with \(N_{p,s}(g)<\infty\), choose a Borel representative and put \(h=g\circ b_p\) on \(\mathbb T_2^p\). For local \(a\in\mathbb Z^p\), define \(\widehat h(a)=2^{-p}\int_{[0,2)^p}h(y)e^{-\mathrm i\pi a^{\mathsf T}y}\,dy\). Then
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathbb Z^p}(1+\pi^2\|a\|_2^2/p)^s
                         |\widehat h(a)|^2\leq N_{p,s}(g)^2.
\]
Consequently, for every \(m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}\), its reflected extension \(F\) satisfies \(\widehat F(0)=0\), \(\widehat F(k)=0\) for \(|\operatorname{supp}(k)|>2\), and
\[
 \sum_{1\leq|\operatorname{supp}(k)|\leq2}
       (1+\pi^2t(k))^s|\widehat F(k)|^2\leq1,
 \qquad \int_{[0,1]^d}|m(x)|^2\,dx\leq1.
\]
All statements are on equivalence classes, with no periodic boundary assumption on the cube function and no ambient-dimension factor in the constant.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: Theorem 1. For every fixed \(s\in(0,1]\), there is \(c_s>0\), independent of \(n,d\), such that for all integers \(n,d\geq2\), \[\inf_{\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}}\mathbb E_\xi\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi,m_\xi)\geq c_s b_s(n,d).\] Consequently \(R_s(n,d)\geq c_s b_s(n,d)\). The coefficient prior is independent of \(X\), and the bound applies to every covariate-dependent randomized sign law in the design class.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: Proposition 1. The laws induced by \(m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}\) and the stated Gaussian causal completion form a proper subclass of \(\mathcal Q_{d,s}\). The design class is the same admissible-kernel class as Cytrynbaum Definition 2.2, specialized to the given covariate distribution and available information. For \(d=2\), Theorem 1 reduces to the single-pair lower exponent \(n^{-s}\); with independent signs, \(\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi,m)=4\mathbb E m(X_1)^2\leq4\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
For all integers \(n,d\geq2\), there is one outcome-independent fair Borel original-sample kernel \(\pi^\star_{n,d}\), independent of \(s\). It assigns independent fair signs if \(B\geq n\). Otherwise it applies Definition \texttt{def:ordered-boundary-rounding} to the first \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) prescribed real features evaluated at the independently reflected and commonly shifted original sample \(W\). The construction uses only \(n,d\), the fixed feature ordering, and fresh independent seeds; it has a finite exact-real algorithm using at most \(n\) moves and uses every original unit with its original HT weight. For every \(0<s\leq1\),
\[
 \pi^\star_{n,d,s}=\pi^\star_{n,d}\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s},\qquad
 a_s(n,d)=\min\{1,(\tbinom d2/n)^s\}=b_s(n,d).
\]
Define the local constant \(c_1\) by
\[
 c_s=\frac{2}{(48+32\pi^2)16384^s}
 \geq c_1:=\frac{2}{(48+32\pi^2)16384}>0,
 \qquad C_s=3072.
\]
The same kernel simultaneously satisfies, for every \(0<s\leq1\),
\[
 c_1a_s(n,d)\leq c_sa_s(n,d)\leq R_s(n,d)
 \leq\sup_{m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}}
       \mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi^\star_{n,d},m)
 \leq3072a_s(n,d).
\]
For each \(s\), the finite coefficient prior \(\nu^\star_{n,d,s}\) of Definition 4, with \(C_0=\sqrt{48+32\pi^2}\), is legal, independent of \(X\), and certifies the sharper lower bound against every design. There is no logarithmic multiplier: below \(B=n\) the scale is \((B/n)^s\), including the endpoint \(s=1\); at and above \(B=n\) it is one. For each fixed \(s\in(0,1]\) and every integer dimension sequence, including oscillating sequences,
\[
 R_s(n,d_n)\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \binom{d_n}{2}/n\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_n=o(\sqrt n).
\]
For a local law \(P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s}\), let \(\mathcal V_n(\pi,P)\) be the actual HT excess with its law-specific benchmark, as defined in Lemma \texttt{lem:published-prognostic-capacity}. The frozen uniform, zero-intercept, correctly specified published class has exactly the same minimax excess capacity:
\[
 \inf_{\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s}}
       \mathcal V_n(\pi,P)=R_s(n,d),
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal Q_{d,s}}\mathcal V_n(\pi^\star_{n,d},P)
 =\sup_{m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}}\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi^\star_{n,d},m)
 \leq3072a_s(n,d).
\]
The Gaussian completions remain a proper law subclass of \(\mathcal Q_{d,s}\). For the larger correctly specified bounded-density class \(\mathcal A_{d,s}\) defined in the same lemma, the transferred conclusion is the all-design converse
\[
 \inf_{\pi\in\mathcal D_{n,d,s}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal A_{d,s}}
       \mathcal V_n(\pi,P)\geq R_s(n,d)\geq c_sa_s(n,d).
\]
For each fixed \(s\), vanishing minimax excess on this larger class therefore requires \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\). No upper bound for nonuniform densities is asserted.

By Lemma \texttt{lem:ht-transfer}, the comparison and the same kernel apply to the stated Gaussian actual HT excess above \(V^*=4.01\). Its worst-case relative excess is at most a specified local \(\varepsilon>0\) whenever
\[
 n\geq B\max\{1,(3072/(4.01\varepsilon))^{1/s}\}.
\]
The optimized worst-case relative excess can be at most \(0<\varepsilon<c_s/4.01\) only if
\[
 n\geq B(c_s/(4.01\varepsilon))^{1/s}.
\]

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
The capacity question has the following complete answer. For every \(n,d\geq2\), set
\[
 a_s(n,d)=\min\{1,(\tbinom d2/n)^s\},\qquad
 \pi^\star_{n,d,s}=\pi^\star_{n,d},\qquad
 \nu^\star_{n,d,s}=\operatorname{Law}(m_\xi)
\]
with the cutoff of Definition \texttt{def:cosine-prior}. The single outcome-independent fair Borel kernel \(\pi^\star_{n,d}\) is independent of \(s\), uses every original unit, and is computed by the stated reflection, common shift, and ordered boundary rounding in at most \(n\) moves. For every \(0<s\leq1\), simultaneously,
\[
 c_sa_s(n,d)\leq R_s(n,d)
 \leq\sup_{m\in\mathcal H_{d,s}}\mathcal L_{n,d,s}(\pi^\star_{n,d},m)
 \leq3072a_s(n,d),\qquad
 c_s=\frac{2}{(48+32\pi^2)16384^s}
       \geq\frac{2}{(48+32\pi^2)16384}>0.
\]
The finite legal prior is independent of \(X\) and certifies the lower bound against every design. Below \(B=n\) the scale is \((B/n)^s\) without logarithmic factors, including \(s=1\) and every subcritical logarithmic window; at and above \(B=n\) it is one. For each fixed \(s\), along every integer dimension sequence,
\[
 R_s(n,d_n)\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \binom{d_n}{2}/n\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_n=o(\sqrt n).
\]
The same inequalities apply to actual Gaussian HT excess above \(4.01\), and the exact minimax-excess capacity of the frozen uniform published class \(\mathcal Q_{d,s}\) equals \(R_s(n,d)\).

items.label: Cited result lem:torus-parseval
items.nl:
For each local positive integer \(r\), the characters \(u\mapsto\exp(2\pi\mathrm i h^{\mathsf T}u)\), \(h\in\mathbb Z^r\), form a complete orthonormal system in \(L^2([0,1)^r)\). Thus, writing \(\widehat f(h)=\int_{[0,1)^r}f(u)\exp(-2\pi\mathrm i h^{\mathsf T}u)\,du\),
\[\|f\|_2^2=\sum_{h\in\mathbb Z^r}|\widehat f(h)|^2,\]
and the Fourier projections onto increasing finite boxes converge in \(L^2\).

items.label: Cited result lem:exact-interpolation-operators
items.nl:
Let \((E_0,E_1)\) and \((G_0,G_1)\) be compatible Banach pairs and \(0<\vartheta<1\). A common linear operator with endpoint bounds \(D:E_h\to G_h\), \(\|D\|\leq A_h<\infty\), \(h=0,1\), has norm at most \(A_0^{1-\vartheta}A_1^\vartheta\) between the corresponding normalized quadratic real-interpolation spaces. The quadratic norm used here is
\[\|v\|_{(E_0,E_1)_{\vartheta,2}}^2=\frac{2\sin(\pi\vartheta)}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\rho^{-1-2\vartheta}\inf_{v=v_0+v_1}\bigl(\|v_0\|_{E_0}^2+\rho^2\|v_1\|_{E_1}^2\bigr)\,d\rho.\]

items.label: Cited result lem:weighted-ltwo-interpolation
items.nl:
On a measure space \((S,\mu)\), let \(w_0,w_1\) be measurable weights strictly positive and finite almost everywhere. For \(0<\vartheta<1\), normalized quadratic real interpolation gives, with equality of norms,
\[(L^2(w_0\,d\mu),L^2(w_1\,d\mu))_{\vartheta,2}=L^2(w_0^{1-\vartheta}w_1^\vartheta\,d\mu).\]
The statement applies to Lebesgue measure and to counting measure.

items.label: Cited result lem:classical-rademacher-contraction
items.nl:
Bartlett--Mendelson Theorem 12(4), with Rademacher complexity as in Definition 2, gives the expected absolute-supremum contraction inequality for an arbitrary function class whenever the displayed expectations are well defined. We use the following sufficient measurability interface. Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_b\) be independent identically distributed local random variables, let \(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_b\) be independent fair signs, and let \(\mathcal G\) consist of measurable real functions. Assume that there is a countable subclass \(\mathcal G_0\subseteq\mathcal G\) such that, for every \(g\in\mathcal G\), finite set \(A\) in the sample space, and \(\varepsilon>0\), some \(g_0\in\mathcal G_0\) satisfies
\[\max_{x\in A}|g_0(x)-g(x)|<\varepsilon,\]
and assume a common integrable envelope \(E\) and one probability-one set on which \(|g(x)|\leq E(x)\) for every \(g\in\mathcal G\). Then every scalar \(1\)-Lipschitz map \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(0)=0\) satisfies
\[\mathbb E\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}\left|\sum_{h=1}^b\rho_h\varphi(g(U_h))\right|\leq2\mathbb E\sup_{g\in\mathcal G}\left|\sum_{h=1}^b\rho_h g(U_h)\right|.\]
The density condition is product-topology density, equivalently simultaneous approximation on every finite evaluation set. We use only \(\varphi(v)=|v|\), finite classes, and the finite-dimensional Euclidean unit-ball linear class.

items.label: Cited result lem:published-ht-excess-identity
items.nl:
Let \(P\) be a local law of \((U,O(0),O(1))\), where \(U\in[0,1]^d\) has a density bounded above and below by finite strictly positive constants and \(\mathbb E_P O(a)^2<\infty\) for \(a=0,1\). Take \(n\) independent copies \((U_i,O_i(0),O_i(1))\). A conditional sign law \(\sigma\) is admissible if it is independent of the potential-outcome array conditional on \(U_{1:n}\) and \(\mathbb E_\sigma[Z_i\mid U_{1:n}]=0\) for every \(i\). Define the local objects
\[
 m_P(u)=\mathbb E_P[(O(1)+O(0))/2\mid U=u],\qquad
 \widehat T_P=\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iO_i((Z_i+1)/2),
\]
\[
 \mathsf V(P)=\operatorname{Var}_P\bigl(\mathbb E_P[O(1)-O(0)\mid U]\bigr)
       +2\mathbb E_P\operatorname{Var}_P(O(1)\mid U)
       +2\mathbb E_P\operatorname{Var}_P(O(0)\mid U).
\]
Then Cytrynbaum's excess-variance identity is
\[
 n\operatorname{Var}_{P,\sigma}(\widehat T_P)-\mathsf V(P)
 =\frac4n\mathbb E_{P,\sigma}\left(\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i m_P(U_i)\right)^2.
\]
All conditional means are interpreted modulo covariate null sets.
